summary: Sound rewrite stage-1 re-measure: the build fix addresses exactly why job 1821bb0e measured master, the target (_moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel x2 at 8.1-9.2 ms, ~5x the 1.67 ms floor) is large and M2 (~470 TFLOP/s) is physically reachable, and the in-process guard removes the child-process rules problem; judge it on the _nvfp4_wgmma_grouped_kernel row, not the headline.
justification: Floor arithmetic checks out: ~16384 local routes x (w13 N=8192 + w2 N=4096) x K=4096 x 2 = ~1.65 TFLOP -> 1.67 ms at 989 TFLOP/s; the Triton incumbent runs at ~200 TFLOP/s (8.1-9.2 ms, 37-57% of every first_turn shape, and first_turn sliding carries weight 138), so even M1 (<6.0 ms) moves the first_turn load ~15%. The design (persistent 288-thread CTAs, 2 consumer WGs on m64n256k16 RS wgmma with weights dequantized into register A fragments, 1 producer warp, 5-stage mbarrier ring, 1-D cp.async.bulk weight blocks pre-permuted in A-fragment order, cp.async 16 B activation gather into the 128B-swizzled K-major B layout) is the standard Hopper mixed-input shape and needs no TMA gather. Turn shapes are untouched by construction (T <= 4096 stays Marlin), so 'neutral' there is right. Weakest link: the kernel has NEVER executed (1821bb0e died in ptxas), so there is zero evidence of correctness or speed; and structurally, the 128 weight-row x 256 token tile re-reads each activation row N/128 times (64x for w13), i.e. ~114 FLOP per smem-filled byte, which needs ~8.6 TB/s of L2->SM activation traffic at peak. That caps this tile shape around 55-70% of peak (L2-bound gather by a single producer warp issuing ~64 cp.async per lane per stage), so M2 (~470 TFLOP/s) is reachable but the ~1.5x-of-floor milestone 3 probably is not without a wider weight tile (e.g. 2 CTAs in a cluster multicasting activations, or 256 weight rows per CTA). Secondary: none of the 5 pre-timing tests reaches T > 4096, so M0's '5/5 tests' says nothing about the CUDA path; its only correctness evidence is prepare's one-hot/e2e self-checks plus the judge's per-call checks on the first_turn timed shapes.
confounders: experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: defines the T > 4096 gate the CUDA path sits behind; not a confounder for the kernel row, but it guarantees turn shapes cannot move, so any turn_1/turn_4 delta is noise.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (w2-nonlocal-zero-store-off-first-turn): the incumbent w2 row is already measured without the ~940 MB zero-store; if the CUDA kernel ignored state['zero_nonlocal_w2'] and zero-stored -1 blocks, a loss would be the port, not the design. Change (3) handles it; verify in the log which value the CUDA call received.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (moe-align-32-experts-first-turn): the incumbent row is timed on the 32-expert align's padded tile count; the CUDA kernel must consume the same sorted_ids/block_experts/n_padded, otherwise its tile count (and row time) is not comparable. Whether this align emits any -1 blocks at all is unclear; the one-hot check covers -1 explicitly either way.
experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256: fixed BLOCK_T 256 for the align padding both engines share; the CUDA kernel's TILE_T 256 matches, so no interaction beyond identical padding.
interference: No companion. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own row (_nvfp4_wgmma_grouped_kernel, 2 calls) against the incumbent _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel's 8083-9174 us on c4d14d62 and against the floor, not on the headline. The landed hypotheses it interacts with only set the inputs (align layout, zero-store flag) that the change explicitly reuses, so reverting or retuning them would change the incumbent and the candidate equally. The PATH CHOSEN / ON / OFF log lines are the internal control: an OFF run is a re-measure of master and is self-identifying. The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: load_inline runs nvcc/ninja as subprocesses; the static checker evidently accepted the previous version (1821bb0e reached ptxas), but keep the build in the same form (no explicit subprocess/multiprocessing in submission.py) so okc_lint and the 'starts processes' check still pass.
Setting os.environ['TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST'] is fine (not editing a loaded module), but restore it in a finally block so a build exception cannot leave it changed for later torch/Triton JIT.
Compile time counts against the 15-minute run budget and, if done in prepare(), the 300 s prepare limit: log compile seconds and keep the Triton fallback reachable within budget.

kernel_fn must not read the device error/abort word or n_padded on the host: _use_cuda_experts must be a prepare()-time flag, and the persistent grid must be sized statically (SM count), not from n_padded, to stay graph-safe with no host sync.

The A-fragment-order permutation plus interleaved block scales is a lossless repack of NVFP4 (codes and e4m3 scales unchanged, global scale applied in fp32 epilogue): allowed. Activations stay BF16 with FP32 accumulation and BF16 output, as the incumbent.

A sticky device fault (illegal address, misaligned bulk copy) in the canary cannot be caught in-process and fails the whole run; that is why the first measurement must be okc check, as the hypothesis says.
open_questions: Does master's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 256, 32) emit any -1 block_experts at all, or does it drop -1 slots entirely? If none are emitted, change (3) is moot for the kernel and the -1 branch is only exercised by the one-hot check.

Do cudaFuncGetAttributes binaryVersion/ptxVersion actually distinguish sm_90 from sm_90a (both report 90)? The __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM90_ALL error-word readback after the canary is the decisive check; the attribute log is only diagnostic.

With 2 consumer WGs each holding a 64x256 fp32 accumulator (128 regs/thread) plus two A-fragment buffers and dequant temporaries, do ptxas registers fit without spills under 288 threads/CTA (setmaxnreg rebalancing)? Log n_regs/local bytes from the attribute query.

For stage 2: is the activation gather (one producer warp, 2048 x 16 B cp.async per stage, 64x re-read for w13) the limiter? Compare the kernel row against ~4 TB/s of L2 activation traffic; if bound there, widen the weight tile (cluster multicast of the B slab or 256 weight rows per CTA) before tuning dequant.

silu-mul-sorted-first-turn is running and first-turn-moe-dead-work-stack / experts-triton-persistent-grid-first-turn are queued on the same T > 4096 path; if any lands first, re-read the incumbent row from the new master before scoring milestones.
